title: Your Email Open Rate Is Lying to You
transcript: The oldest tool on the internet still makes the most money, and most marketers are using it wrong. Email beats every channel marketers obsess over. Higher conversions than paid social, higher conversions than paid search, higher conversions than almost anything you can spend money on. But, here's the problem. Everyone's measuring it wrong. They look at open rates. Open rates only tell part of the story. It tells you that someone glanced at your subject line, and maybe saw a little bit of your email, but it doesn't tell you if they did anything about it. The number [music] that actually predicts revenue is click-through rate, and the data on this is wild. The industry average across platforms is between 0.9% [music] and 2.5%. The top performers, they're hitting 6.3%. That's five to seven times the average. So, what are the top performers actually doing differently? Comes down [music] to one thing, copy. The brands hitting 6% click-through rate aren't getting lucky. They treat their copy like a testable variable. They use AI to generate five [music] to six variations of their email. They AB test them, they see what's actually getting clicked, then they iterate. That's why platforms like HighLevel, where the AI copy generation and the AB testing live within [music] inside the tool, are pulling those numbers. Not because the platform is magic, but because the workflow is. Stop just tracking opens, start testing copy. Your click-through rate is a revenue number that matters.
